randomizer_settings.label: Settings preset
randomizer_settings.description:
Selecting a preset will replace all randomizer settings to make them follow the selected preset, which can either be a randomizer built-in preset or a custom one. If you have made unsaved changes to your randomizer settings, be sure to save them before selecting a preset, in order to avoid losing them.
Built-in randomizer presets currently include the following:
- Default: the default settings for the randomizer, including Basic skill assumptions and Normal item progression. This is highly recommended for first-time players.
- Community Racing Season 3: the settings currently used in community races, including Hard skill assumptions, Tricky item progression with 2 additional Super packs, and "Save the animals" required.
To create a new custom preset, use the "Save Settings" button at the bottom of the page. To manage existing custom presets, click the gear button to the right of the preset selection.
randomizer_settings.notes: Website form field 'full_settings_preset' (select, id fullSettingsPreset). Option list: placeholder '' ('Select a preset to automatically fill all settings'), then any user custom presets (stored in browser localforage 'customPresets'), then the built-in full presets in order. Selecting a preset applies all its settings. Changing any setting afterwards resets the select to '' (sent as name="" ; JSON type is Option<String>). Server-side (assign_presets), if name matches a built-in full preset, the whole settings object is replaced by that preset when apply_presets is true.

randomizer_settings.label: Skill assumptions
randomizer_settings.description:
Skill assumptions determine which tricks the randomizer assumes the player is able to perform. This affects where the randomizer may place key items on any given step. Anything selected here is "fair game" for the player to be required to do in order to progress.
After selecting one of the preset difficulty levels, it is possible to refine it by clicking the gear button on the right and modifying the selections. Note that if you then select a preset again, it will override any customized settings that you made.
The descriptions below are only a brief summary. Clicking the gear button will show a list of all the tricks in detail, with animations. It's recommended to take a look to make sure you understand all the kinds of things that you may be expected to be able to do!
Examples of expected techniques from the skill presets are as follows:
- Basic: Wall jumps, shinesparks, simple uses of frozen enemies, and navigating heated rooms without Varia (but only with plenty of extra energy).
- Medium: 1-tap shortcharge, short infinite bomb jumps, sequences of 3 or more wall jumps, and underwater movement tech such as crouch jumps, down grabs, mid-air Spring Ball jumps, and Gravity jumps.
- Hard: 2-tap shortcharge, horizontal mid-air shinesparks, mockballs, gate glitching, trickier climbing on enemies, ice clips assisted by Morph and X-Ray, cross-room jumps from air to water rooms, and using a turn-around to jump around a corner.
- Very Hard: Stutter 3-tap, complex shinespark setups, stutter water shortcharges, speedballs, temporary blue suit, horizontal damage boosts, Spring Ball jumps off of walls, Flatley jumps, evading Metroids, short X-ray climbs, CWJ with retries.
- Expert: Stutter 4-tap, double Spring Ball jumps, precise ice clips, temporary blue chains, pause abuse, grapple jumps, spring flings, and very precise jumps that get extra height with Speed Booster.
- Expert+: Bypassing locked door shells, glitched X-ray modes (G-mode, R-mode, X-mode), blue suits (Crystal Spark, R-mode spark interrupt), and flash suits (spikesuit, R-mode CF interrupt).
- Extreme: Double-stutter 4-tap, underwater wall jumps, moonfalls between frozen enemies, X-mode blue suits, R-mode standup clips, and complex G-mode applications (such as upward setups and artificial morph).
- Extreme+: Moondances, bootless double Spring Ball jumps underwater with Bombs, diagonal bomb jumps, utilizing the initial spark when gaining a flash suit, back-to-back X-mode to gain a blue suit, and G-mode into and from heat.
- Insane: Triple-stutter 4-tap, Taco Tank, elevator Crystal Flash, slope sparks, downward G-mode setups, moondances that require exact counts, and very slow and unforgiving strats.
- Insane+: Crossing Colosseum with no movement items, ceiling bomb jumps, free fall clips, bootless UWJ within a two-tile wide gap, super sinks, first-try spike suits, and R-mode knockback sparks.

randomizer_settings.label: Item progression
randomizer_settings.description:
Item progression settings affect the rate at which the randomizer will place key items, and which locations it will place them in, within the constraints of the selected "Skill assumptions" above. Four presets are available:
- Normal: Key items are placed generously: by the time 50% of items are obtainable, at least 75% of key items should be obtainable. Morph, Bombs, and an ETank are placed early. Key items have no specific tendency to be in harder or easier locations to reach. Beams, additional tanks, and ammo are spread out uniformly. Multiple progression options are generally possible from relatively early in the game.
- Tricky: Key items are spread out at a roughly uniform pace but tend to be placed in harder-to-reach locations. Beams, tanks, and ammo are spread out uniformly as filler. Multiple progression options are generally possible by the middle of the game.
- Technical: Key items are delayed and tend to be placed in harder-to-reach locations. Tanks and certain beams (Charge, Wave, Spazer) are spread out as filler. Access to ammo other than Missiles is often delayed. A single progression sequence may be forced until late in the game.
- Challenge: Key items are delayed similarly to "Technical", but access to tanks is often delayed. Charge and Spazer are the only beams placed as filler. A single progression sequence may be forced until late in the game.
- Desolate: Some key items may not be placed at all, and the amount of ammo and tanks is greatly reduced. A single progression sequence may be forced through almost the entire game.
For players new to this randomizer, the "Normal" preset is highly recommended. The "Tricky" preset and higher settings tend to make the game significantly more difficult. The "Technical" setting is recommended for players who want to be forced to learn new techniques to progress. Be careful selecting "Challenge" or "Desolate" settings as these can be fairly punishing: they are likely to require the player to go without Energy Tanks for much of the game.
"Item progression" and "Skill assumptions" synergize with one another: harder item progression settings increase the likelihood that harder techniques selected in the "Skill assumptions" will actually be required to beat the game.
The item progression settings can be customized by clicking the gear button on the right. Note that selecting a preset again will override any customized selections.
randomizer_settings.notes: Website form field 'item_progression_preset' (radio buttons on main page, HTML pre-checked 'Normal'), plus a gear button opening the Item Progression modal. Presets from data/presets/item-progression/{Normal,Tricky,Technical,Challenge,Desolate}.json. Changing any item-progression sub-setting unchecks all buttons -> null (custom). Note: when start location 'Escape' is selected the preset buttons are visually flagged as conflicting (starting items are forced to all).

randomizer_settings.label: Progression rate
randomizer_settings.description:
This setting affects the quantity of key items that the randomizer places on each step:
- Fast: Key items are placed at double that of a uniform rate, concentrating them in locations accessible earlier in the game. By the time 50% of items are obtainable, at least 75% of key items should be obtainable.
- Uniform: Key items are placed at a uniform rate. By the middle of the game there will likely be many possible ways to progress.
- Slow: At most one key item is placed at each step. This tends to limit the player to a linear progression sequence, with many key items not being accessible until near the end of the game.
Details
With a Uniform progression rate, on a given step, the proportion of item locations to fill with key items (as opposed to filler items) is targeted to match the fraction of key items among all unplaced items; in other words, the amount of key items to be placed is roughly equal to the expected (average) amount if items were to be drawn completely randomly from the pool of unplaced items.
On Slow progression, on each step the randomizer will first attempt to place zero key items, in case the filler items alone may be sufficient to provide progression. If that fails, it will try placing one key item.
randomizer_settings.notes: Website form field 'progression_rate' (radio buttons). No option is pre-checked in the HTML (value set from the loaded preset). Choices rendered from progression_rates = ['Fast','Uniform','Slow'] (main.rs).

randomizer_settings.label: Item placement
randomizer_settings.description:
This setting affect how the randomizer selects locations to place key items in on each step, among all the possible obtainable item locations as determined by "Skill assumptions".
- Neutral: Key items are placed in random locations (among the possible locations).
- Forced: Key items tend to be placed in locations requiring difficult techniques to reach.
- Local: Key items tend to be placed in locations requiring difficult techniques to reach, and in case of a tie in difficulty, preference is given to a location in the same area as a key item on the previous step.
randomizer_settings.notes: Website form field 'item_placement_style' (radio buttons). HTML pre-checked value before presets load: "Neutral".

randomizer_settings.label: Item priority strength
randomizer_settings.description:
This setting affects how strongly the randomizer follows the item priority settings in placing key items:
- Moderate: The randomizer will usually prioritize placing "Early" items early and "Late" items late, but not always.
- Heavy: The randomizer will always prioritize placing "Early" items early and "Late" items late, only selecting an item with later priority when no other choice provides progression.
Details
With the "Moderate" setting, at the start of each seed generation attempt, the randomizer randomly shuffles the list of key items, with two copies of "Early" and "Late" items being included: for "Early" items, whichever copy occurs earlier is kept, while for "Late" items, whichever copy comes later is kept, to determine the item priority order.
With the "Heavy" setting, the "Early" items are shuffled among themselves, "Default" items are shuffled among themselves, and "Late" items are shuffled among themselves; these three lists are then concatenated together to determine the item priority order.
randomizer_settings.notes: Website form field 'item_priority_strength' (radio buttons). HTML pre-checked value before presets load: "Moderate".

randomizer_settings.label: Random tank priority
randomizer_settings.description:
This setting affects how the key item priority order of Energy Tank vs. Reserve Tank works from step to step:
- No: All items, including Energy Tanks and Reserve Tanks, maintain a consistent item priority across steps. This means it is more likely that you only get one type of tank for much of the seed (especially if tanks are not enabled as filler items).
- Yes: The priority of Energy Tanks and Reserve Tanks, relative to each other, is re-randomized on every step. This makes it more likely that you get a mixture of the two types of tanks.
randomizer_settings.notes: Website form field 'random_tank' (radio, values 'false'/'true'). HTML pre-checked: true.

randomizer_settings.label: Spazer before Plasma
randomizer_settings.description: If enabled, Spazer will be prioritized before Plasma both as a key item and as filler (if applicable). This makes it more likely that Spazer would be obtainable before Plasma. It could still happen that both beams are placed on the same step, or that Plasma is placed first if it would provide progression when Spazer would not.
randomizer_settings.notes: Website form field 'spazer_before_plasma' (radio, values 'false'/'true'). HTML pre-checked: true. Flagged as conflicting on the website if Spazer or Plasma is removed from the item pool.

randomizer_settings.label: Ammo collect fraction
randomizer_settings.description:
This determines what fraction of logically collectible ammo packs the player may be required to collect. This affects Missiles, Supers, and Power Bombs. It should be set to a value between 0.5 and 1.0. For each type of ammo, the number of packs that are logically collectible is multiplied by this fraction, then rounded to the nearest integer, to determine the amount of packs assumed by the logic to have been collected.
Setting this fraction to 1.0 means that everything available is assumed to be collected, which means that in some scenarios the player could be required to sweep the world to collect every available pack. The default value of 0.7 ensures that the player will have more flexibility. The following table shows how the number of available packs of a given type (Missiles, Supers, or Power Bombs) corresponds to the number of packs assumed by the logic to be collected, based on the default of 0.7:
Collectible packs | Assumed collected packs
0 | 0
1 | 1
2 | 1

randomizer_settings.section: Item progression > Item Progression modal > Key item priority
randomizer_settings.label: Key item priority
randomizer_settings.description:
These settings affect how the randomizer prioritizes placing key items, which can be used to nudge the randomizer to try to place certain items earlier or later on average. Wide variation should still be expected in the results, because of constraints that limit how early or late the randomizer can place a key item in any given situation, especially for lower settings of "Skill assumptions".
Details
At the beginning of each randomization attempt, an item priority order is determined by randomly shuffling all the item types, with a bias such that "Early" items (as selected below) tend to come before "Default" items, which in turn tend to come before "Late" items. Every item type occurs somewhere in this priority order (even Missiles and other filler items), with the exception of "Never" items. The same priority order is used across all steps of a given attempt.
On a given step, the randomizer determines the quantity of key items to place based on the "Progression rate". It will always begin by attempting to place the first available key item(s) from the priority order in two-way reachable locations, along with randomly selected filler items. The randomizer places filler items in one-way reachable locations. If the selected combination of items provides progression, then the randomizer will accept this placement and move on to the next step. Otherwise, the randomizer replaces the last key item with the next one in the priority order and tries again, continuing this way until it either succeeds or all item types are exhausted, in which case it will try again with a new map and new item priority order.
randomizer_settings.notes: JSON: list of {"item": Item, "priority": "Early"|"Default"|"Late"} (KeyItemPriority). One radio group 'item_priority_<Item>' per prioritizable item, in this order: ETank, ReserveTank, Super, PowerBomb, Charge, Ice, Wave, Spazer, Plasma, XRayScope, Morph, Bombs, Grapple, HiJump, SpeedBooster, SparkBooster, BlueBooster, SpringBall, WallJump, SpaceJump, ScrewAttack, Varia, Gravity. Every item offers exactly Early / Default / Late (HTML pre-checked Default). Missile is not listed (always filler). Items with 0 count in the pool are flagged as conflicting.

randomizer_settings.section: Item progression > Item Progression modal > Filler items
randomizer_settings.label: Filler items
randomizer_settings.description:
This setting affects which items will be treated as filler items:
- No: The item is not treated as filler. This means it will only be placed if it is placed as a key item (e.g. if it helps provide progression), or at the end of item placement when the remaining items are placed.
- Semi: The item is not initially treated as filler. Once the first instance of the item is obtainable, additional instances become filler on subsequent steps.
- Yes: This item is treated as filler. This means it is mixed into the pool of items, along with Missiles, to fill up item locations on each step, without regard to whether it provides progression.
- Early: This item is treated as filler, and one instance of the item will be prioritized to be placed as early as possible.
Filler items are randomly mixed in with Missiles to fill up the remaining obtainable item locations on each randomization step (ones not already being filled by key items).
For example, assuming Power Bombs are not selected as a filler item, then the game will only place the first Power Bomb pack as a key item (providing progression), but afterwards it will randomly mix the remaining Power Bomb packs in with the Missiles even if they don't provide further progression.

One radio group 'filler_items_<Item>' per prioritizable item (same order as key_item_priority). 'Semi' is offered ONLY for Super, PowerBomb, ETank, ReserveTank; all other items offer No / Yes / Early. No HTML pre-checked value (filled from preset). Missile is not listed (always filler).

randomizer_settings.label: Quality-of-life options
randomizer_settings.description:
These options help provide a smoother, more intuitive, and less tedious game experience. Several presets are provided:
- Off: All quality-of-life options are turned off. This is for players who want a full experience of exploration, with a similar feel to the original game. This may involve a lot of wandering around and backtracking to figure out where to go. Map stations are harder to find and provide minimal assistance as all item dots look the same.
- Low: Many quality-of-life options are turned off, restoring some unintuitive but potentially interesting vanilla game behavior: some items do not spawn until defeating Phantoon or waking the planet, Acid Chozo statue requires Space Jump to use it, and completing the escape may require collecting certain items and/or carefully managing energy in the Mother Brain fight. Map stations are somewhat less powerful because all ammo and tank items appear as small dots the same as Missiles.
- Default: Quality-of-life options are turned to their generally recommended settings (mostly on). Map stations are very useful, with different item dot shapes to distinguish three tiers of items: Missiles, other ammo/tank items, and unique items. Enemy drops are somewhat improved, reducing the need for long farms.
- High: Map stations reveal even more information: ammo items (Supers and Power Bombs) are shown with a a small "X" while Energy Tanks and Reserve Tanks are shown with an "O". Map stations also reveal area connections in neighboring areas, showing how they connect back to the current area. Energy stations and E-Tanks also refill reserve energy, and E-Tanks can be disabled.
- Max: All quality-of-life options are turned on to their highest settings. This includes respin, lenient Space Jump, and momentum conservation to more fluidly control Samus, and an extra-fast Mother Brain fight that completely skips the second and third phases. Energy can also be manually transferred back into reserve tanks.
Individual options may be customized by clicking the gear button on the right.

randomizer_settings.label: Item markers
randomizer_settings.description:
This option affects the way that items are drawn on the map (pause menu map and HUD minimap). There are four choices:
- Simple: All items are marked on the map with small dots.
- Majors: Unique items, E-Tanks, and Reserve Tanks are marked with large solid dots; other items are marked with small dots.
- Uniques: Unique items are marked with large solid dots; other items are marked with small dots.
- 3-Tiered: Unique items are marked with large solid dots; Supers, Power Bombs, E-Tanks, and Reserve Tanks are marked with large hollow dots; Missiles are marked with small dots.
- 4-Tiered: Unique items are marked with large solid dots; E-Tanks and Reserve Tanks are marked with large hollow dots; Supers and Power Bombs are marked with small X's; Missiles are marked with small dots.
If you like doing more exploration, you may want to select an option providing less information.

randomizer_settings.description:
If enabled, entering a room causes the outline of the room to be revealed in the pause map. Tiles which have only been revealed in this way are shown in the pause map with a black interior. Room details such as item dots or door locks are not shown. This feature is limited to the pause map and has no effect on the HUD mini-map.
This option can make it easier for players to remember the rooms they have visited and to see how they connect.

randomizer_settings.label: Opposite area transitions revealed by map

If enabled, activating a map stations causes area-transition markers (arrows or letters) to be revealed in neighboring areas, showing connections leading back to the area where the map station was activated.
This option can make it easier for players to visualize how areas connect together.
Note that regardless of this setting, map stations always reveal area-transition markers in the area where the map station was activated, showing outgoing connections to other areas. Also, crossing an area transition always reveals both sides of the connection.

- Vanilla: The fight behaves as in the vanilla game. Some cutscenes are accelerated, but only in ways that should not interfere with how the player executes the fight (including the stand-up glitch).
- Short: The third phase of the fight is skipped.
- Skip: The second and third phases of the fight are skipped.
With the "Short" and "Skip" options, Samus will not get an energy refill before the escape, as the cutscene is skipped where the refill would normally happen. However, Samus will always collect Hyper Beam.

randomizer_settings.label: Supers do double damage to Mother Brain

If enabled, Supers will deal double damage to Mother Brain, applying to all three phases of the fight.
Given that the randomizer does not change the ammo distribution (there are only 50 Supers in the game), this option reduces the need for a long "ammo hunt" before fighting Mother Brain if the player has not found Charge Beam.
This option can be set independently of the "Mother Brain fight" setting, though in case of a "Short" Mother Brain fight, its practical effect is minimal.

If disabled and failing to escape then Samus will respawn at the last used save point and have to defeat Mother Brain again to attempt the escape.

- Spring Ball
- Screw Attack
- Hi-Jump Boots
- Space Jump
- Speed Booster
- Grapple
- X-Ray
- WallJump (if applicable)
The escape timer is based on an assumption that the player has all these items available. By granting them with Hyper Beam, it avoids the possibility of the player needing to hunt for movement items in order to complete the escape fast enough.
Note: Regardless of this setting, in this randomizer Hyper Beam always breaks bomb blocks, Super blocks, and Power Bomb blocks and can open blue/green gates from either side.
If the item progression option "Stop item placement early" is enabled (for example in "Desolate"), then all movement items will be given during the escape, regardless of the option "Hyper Beam gives all movement items" is enabled or not.

randomizer_settings.section: Quality-of-life options > Tweaks to unintuitive vanilla behavior
randomizer_settings.label: All items spawn at start of game
randomizer_settings.description:
In the vanilla game, some items do not spawn until certain conditions are fulfilled:
- Items in Wrecked Ship rooms (with the exception of the one item in Wrecked Ship Main Shaft) do not spawn until after Phantoon is defeated, when the rooms change to appearing "powered on".
- The item in the left side of Morph Ball Room and in The Final Missile do not spawn until the planet is awakened.
- The item in Pit Room does not spawn until entering with Morph and Missiles collected (regardless of whether the planet is awake).
These conditions are apparently unintended artifacts of how the game was coded and are not normally observable during casual play of the vanilla game. However, they can frequently be observed in the randomizer, which can be counter-intuitive for players. When this quality-of-life option is enabled, these items will spawn from the beginning of the game instead of requiring those conditions.
How to awaken the planet
Whether or not this option is enabled, the way to awaken the planet is same as in the vanilla game: it is done by unlocking any gray door that requires killing enemies in the room (not including bosses). In the randomizer currently there are four rooms where this can be done:
- Pit Room (old Mother Brain room)
- Baby Kraid Room
- Metal Pirates
- Plasma Room
Note that in order to awaken the planet using the Pit Room, the player must enter the room with Morph and Missiles, otherwise the enemies and gray doors would not spawn.
Additional Notes
Other vanilla effects of defeating Phantoon and waking the planet are unaffected by this option, including:
- After defeating Phantoon, the Bowling Alley Chozo statue becomes usable and there are changes to enemy spawns. This includes the Workrobot which will move and open access to the item in Wrecked Ship East Super Room.
- After the planet is awakened, enemies will spawn in Parlor, Climb, Construction Zone, Morph Ball Room, and Blue Brinstar Energy Tank Room.
randomizer_settings.notes: Website form field 'all_items_spawn' (radio buttons). HTML pre-checked value before presets load: true.

randomizer_settings.section: Quality-of-life options > Tweaks to unintuitive vanilla behavior

randomizer_settings.label: Crash fixes
randomizer_settings.description:
Change the behaviour of how game crashes are handled. This feature can prevent a hardlock if any of the following bugs are triggered:
- Spring Ball bounce: Triggered by pausing and unequipping Spring Ball at certain points in the middle of a neutral bounce.
- Yapping Maw shinespark: If a Yapping Maw tries to grab Samus during a shinespark, followed by having no inputs held during the shinespark end.
- Frame perfect pause, autoreserve: Having autoreserves trigger on the exact frame the screen finishes fading out while pausing.
- X-Mode tile collision: Colliding with a solid tile during X-Mode.
- Sprite overflow bug: Leaving a room with 32 sprites loaded.
Individual customization options are available by clicking the gear button on the right.
- Crash: When triggered, only the vanilla code will run. This will cause a hardlock of the game.
- Death: When triggered, a dialog box will appear explaining the crash followed by triggering a death sequence / game-over, preventing the vanilla hardlock.
- Warn: When triggered, a dialog box will appear explaining the crash but game play will continue after the dialog box is closed.
- Silent: When triggered, no dialog box will appear and the game will continue as if the crash hadn't been triggered.
Details
The sprite overflow bug does not have a message box if set to death due to the bug happening in the door transition. For the same reason there is no warn option for this bug. Default behaviour for all presets other than crash is to silently fix the bug. If death is desired it can be manually enabled using the gear icon.
In underwater physics, the Spring Ball bounce crash is triggered when Spring Ball is unequipped at any point while Samus is moving upward from the neutral bounce. In air physics, it happens when Spring Ball is unequipped on an exact frame when landing from the neutral bounce.
randomizer_settings.notes: Website form field 'crash_fixes_preset' (radio buttons). HTML pre-checked value before presets load: "Death". JSON Option<CrashFixesPreset>. Crash: all five set Crash. Death: spring_ball/yapping_maw/auto_reserve/x_mode Death, sprite_overflow Silent. Warn: four set Warn, sprite_overflow Silent. Silent: all Silent. Editing an individual fix (gear -> Crash fixes modal) unchecks all -> null. Server-side upgrade: if preset is set, all individual fields are recomputed from it (CrashFixes::from_preset).

randomizer_settings.section: Quality-of-life options > Ammo, energy, and reserves
randomizer_settings.label: Reserve energy backward transfer
randomizer_settings.description:
If enabled, the player may transfer regular energy into reserve tanks. After setting the reserve tank mode to MANUAL, press D-Pad Left to move the cursor to the large arrow. Press the A button and the arrow will switch directions.
The arrow indicates which way energy will transfer when the "RESERVE TANK" item is activated: normally it points from the reserve tank up to regular energy, and it will always return to this state when leaving the equipment menu (to view the map or to unpause). When toggled, it will instead point down, from regular energy, into the reserve tank. Thus, energy will be transferred from regular energy tanks to reserve tanks.
When using this feature, if reserve energy is overfilled, then regular energy instantly depletes to 1, similar to the vanilla behavior which instantly depletes reserve energy to 0 when regular energy is overfilled.

randomizer_settings.label: Enemy drops
randomizer_settings.description:
This option affects the drops spawned by enemies:
- Off: Enemies do not spawn drops.
The "Off" option is not fully implemented in the logic: it may result in unbeatable seeds.
- Vanilla: Enemies spawn drops as in the vanilla game.
- Buffed: Enemies spawn drops with improved probabilities and values, as described below.
If buffed drops are enabled, then the following improvements are made to enemy drops:
- Small energy drops give 10 energy.
- Power Bomb drops give 2 Power Bombs.
- Respawning enemies drop Power Bombs at double the normal rate. This affects Gamets, Zebs, Geegas, Zebbos, Zoas, and Coverns.
- Zebs, Geegas, and Kagos drop Supers at double the normal rate.
Details
The increased Power Bomb and Super drop probabilities come out of the Nothing, Missile, and Small Energy drop probabilities. Large Energy drop rates are increased to compensate for the loss of some Small Energy drop probability. The doubled Power Bomb drop probabilities combines with the increased drop value (each Power Bomb drop giving 2 Power Bombs) to result in an overall quadrupled rate of Power Bomb farming. The resulting drop probabilities are shown in the following table:
Enemy | Nothing | Small Energy | Large Energy | Missile | Super | Power Bomb
Gamet | 2% | 24% | 24% | 20% | 24% | 8%
Zeb | 0% | 8% | 26% | 12% | 48% | 8%
Geega | 0% | 8% | 26% | 12% | 48% | 8%
Zebbo | 0% | 0% | 56% | 2% | 40% | 4%
Zoa | 2% | 0% | 40% | 24% | 28% | 8%
Covern | 0% | 20% | 38% | 20% | 8% | 16%
Kago | 2% | 14% | 38% | 24% | 16% | 8%

randomizer_settings.label: Map layout
randomizer_settings.description:
This setting affects how the rooms are arranged on the map:
- Vanilla: The rooms are arranged as they are in the vanilla game, i.e. there is no map randomization. Consider checking out VARIA Randomizer, which has more specialized support for vanilla map.
- Small: Only a subset of the rooms are included in the game, based on Standard maps but with some areas removed.
- Standard: The rooms are arranged in a random but relatively friendly way: one-ways tend to have short return paths that loop back around.
- Wild: The rooms are arranged in a more random and less friendly way: there will often be one-ways with only long return paths.
Be aware that randomized maps (even "Standard" ones) tend to be much more difficult than the vanilla map: expect to encounter frequent risks of death & softlock, particularly at the beginning of the game. "Standard" maps should typically be relatively straightforward to navigate once you have collected enough items, but reaching that point probably won't be easy. "Wild" maps are even more spicy and tend to contain some very long one-way loops (like the Lower Norfair loop in the vanilla map, or even longer).
When using Vanilla map, it is suggested to use "Neutral" item progression (instead of "Forced") since otherwise the location of key items may be overly predictable.
With Small maps, a handful of doors will be replaced with walls. Any objectives which do not exist in the map will be excluded and will not appear in the pause menu objective screen.
Details
On all settings, the randomizer guarantees that one-ways (such as falling through crumble blocks) always loop back around somehow, though the path back could be long and require certain items. This setting ("Standard" vs. "Wild") affects the typical length of such paths.
The "one-ways" considered here are situations where navigation in a "wrong" direction might not be not possible within the room, even with all items collected, without the use of techniques above Basic:
- Crumble blocks in Spore Spawn Super Room, Green Pirates Shaft, Big Pink, and many other rooms.
- Sand transitions.
- Green gates (whether or not they are glitchable).
- Speed blocks in Crateria Super Room and Crocomire Speedway.
- Big Pink morph tunnel Super block.
- Acid in Amphitheatre.
- The barriers in Spore Spawn's Room, Crocomire's Room, and Botwoon's Room.
- Acid and solid block in Acid Statue Room.
- Bowling Alley Chozo.
- The walls separating the Main Street morph tunnel from the rest of the room (a "zero-way").
- Mother Brain Room and Bowling Alley (top vs. rest) are also treated as zero-way.
Likewise, in measuring the length of paths to reverse a "one-way", the types of paths considered are those which will be possible with all items collected but without the use of techniques above Basic.

- Blue: All doors are blue, except for gray doors.
- Ammo: Red, green, and yellow doors are randomly mixed in.
- Beam: Beam doors are randomly mixed in, replacing some of the ammo doors.
Gray doors are unaffected by this setting and always exist in the same set of rooms: boss/miniboss rooms and the four Pirates rooms (Pit Room, Baby Kraid Room, Plasma Room, and Metal Pirates Room).
For ammo and beam doors, both sides of the door will have the same color and share a lock, so that unlocking one side of the door also unlocks the other.
Ammo and beam doors will not be placed on or immediately connect to any special tile such as a save, map, refill, objective "X", or a gray door.
Click on the gear icon to customize the number of ammo and beam doors that can appear. This sets the maximum number of doors, and the randomizer will attempt to place that many. In certain cases, fewer doors than the maximum can be placed.

- Door leading left to the top of Ridley's Room.

randomizer_settings.description:
When this option is enabled, the game no longer patches out major glitches:
- "GT Code": holding A, B, X, and Y when entering Golden Torizo's Room grants the player 700 Energy, 300 Reserve Energy, 100 Missiles, 20 Supers, 20 Power Bombs, and every unique item in the game except for Screw Attack and X-Ray.
- Glitched beams: The player may equip Spazer and Plasma simultaneously, resulting in glitched effects when firing.
- Out of bounds: Samus may move outside the rectangular bounds of the room without triggering death.
Use this setting with caution, as major glitches may crash the game, corrupt the save file, or cause the game to become unbeatable. There is no guarantee that major glitches will behave the same as they do in the vanilla game.
This option is always enabled when using "Ultra-low quality of life".

randomizer_settings.label: Race mode
randomizer_settings.description:
When set to "Yes", spoiler data is initially locked. The creator of the seed can unlock the spoiler data, at which point it will become viewable to everyone, and the timestamp when the spoiler data was unlocked will be shown on seed page.
The seed creator will need to use the same device and browser to unlock the spoiler data as what they used to create it (as the ability to unlock the data depends on a small random token in browser-local storage).
randomizer_settings.notes: Website form field 'race_mode' (radio buttons). HTML pre-checked value before presets load: false.

randomizer_settings.label: Enable savestates
randomizer_settings.description:
This in-game save state option allows creating at most one save state at a time. A save state can be loaded an unlimited amount of times. Any save state is cleared automatically by a regular save (at a save station or the Ship).
- Unlimited: A save state can be created at any time.
- Limited: A save state can be created only once, until refreshed by a regular save or load.
Compared to emulator/platform-based save states, the in-game save state option has some advantages:
- Map tile progress is maintained.
- Music continues uninterrupted if the track is unchanged.
- Item collection times and other stats are preserved.
- The fact that save states are cleared by regular saves can help prevent accidental loads.
- The "Limited" option, if enabled, forces strategic use of save states.
- It works for some platforms (e.g FXPAK) that would otherwise be unsupported.
This feature requires 256KB SRAM; FXPAK and most modern emulators support this configuration.

If this field is left blank (or if Race Mode is enabled), then the randomizer will automatically choose a random seed.

- Reduced: Most large, sudden flashes are reduced to have a milder change in brightness, while still being noticeable. Caution is recommended for those with serious sensitivities to such effects, as the effectiveness of these changes is not guaranteed and may vary by individual.
The full-screen flashing after Mother Brain phase 1 is an exception, being always removed regardless of which option is selected.

- Disabled: The low-energy beeping is disabled.

customize_settings.section: Seed page > Customization > Other customization options
customize_settings.label: Room palettes
customize_settings.description:
This setting controls the palettes for rooms (affecting foregrounds and backgrounds):
- Vanilla: Rooms use the palette from the original game.
- Area-themed: Each room uses a palette based on its area in the randomized map.
- Area-shuffled: Each area is randomly assigned one of the six area palette themes, with every palette used exactly once.
- Scrambled: Each room uses a random selection of one of six possible palettes.
- If an individual area is selected (e.g. Crateria), then all rooms use a palette based on that area.
customize_settings.notes: Select 'room_palettes' (id roomPalettes); an <hr> separates the first four options from the per-area constant palettes. Server mapping: area-themed->AreaThemed, area-shuffled->AreaShuffled, scrambled->Scrambled, vanilla->Vanilla, crateria/brinstar/norfair/wrecked-ship/maridia/tourian -> PaletteTheme::Constant(0..5). Default effectively 'vanilla' (also set by room_theming 'tiling' default).

customize_settings.section: Seed page > Customization > Other customization options
customize_settings.label: Tile theme
customize_settings.description:
This setting controls how the rooms in the game will be drawn. This affects only the graphical appearance of the rooms.
- If Vanilla is selected, then rooms are tiled as they are in the vanilla game.
- If Area-themed is selected, then rooms are tiled according to their area on the map.
- If Area-shuffled is selected, then the tile themes are randomly shuffled across the six areas. Rooms within an area retain consistent subarea theming.
- If Scrambled is selected, then each room is tiled using a random theme.
- If an individual theme is selected (e.g. Outer Crateria), then all the rooms are tiled using that theme.
- If Practice Outlines is selected, then rooms are tiled using green outlines to mark the room collision; special blocks are shown in their true form; and a background grid helps with measuring positions and distances.
- If Invisible is selected, then rooms are tiled using blank, transparent foreground, making the game difficult to navigate. Doors will still be visible, as will vanilla backgrounds and sprites.
With Area-themed, Area-shuffled, or Scrambled modes, rooms that directly connect to Tourian will use the Statues Hallway theme. For Area-themed and Area-shuffled modes, any single-doored room next to such a room will also use the Statues Hallway theme.
customize_settings.notes: Select 'tile_theme' (id tileTheme). HTML pre-selected 'none', but on page load room_theming defaults to 'tiling' which sets tile_theme to 'area_themed' (so the effective default is 'area_themed'). Server mapping: none->Vanilla, scrambled->Scrambled, area_themed->AreaThemed, area_shuffled->AreaShuffled, anything else -> TileTheme::Constant(<value>) (mosaic theme names from main.rs mosaic_themes, plus StatuesHallway, Outline, Invisible). <hr> separators after Scrambled and after Statues Hallway.

- Revamped: Each reserve tank is indicated with a bar showing how full it is. If reserve mode is AUTO, then the AUTO text also appears, and its color indicates whether reserves have any energy or not.

customize_settings.section: Seed page > Customization > Other customization options
customize_settings.label: Screw Attack animation
customize_settings.description:
This setting determines how the Screw Attack animation appears:
- Vanilla: The Screw Attack animation is always based on the Space Jump animation regardless of whether or not Space Jump is equipped.
- Split: Screw Attack without Space Jump equipped is based on the spin-jump animation. Screw Attack with Space Jump equipped is based on the Space Jump animation.
The behavior of the vanilla game can be explained by the fact that the player was expected to obtain Space Jump before Screw Attack and never have a reason to unequip Space Jump. Hence the possibility of using Screw Attack without Space Jump was apparently overlooked or considered unimportant.

customize_settings.section: Seed page > Customization > Other customization options > Controller settings > Save state
customize_settings.label: Save state: X
customize_settings.description:
This in-game save state option allows creating at most one save state at a time. A save state can be loaded an unlimited amount of times. Any save state is cleared automatically by a regular save (at a save station or the Ship).
- Unlimited: A save state can be created at any time.
- Limited: A save state can be created only once, until refreshed by a regular save or load.
Compared to emulator/platform-based save states, the in-game save state option has some advantages:
- Map tile progress is maintained.
- Music continues uninterrupted if the track is unchanged.
- Item collection times and other stats are preserved.
- The fact that save states are cleared by regular saves can help prevent accidental loads.
- The "Limited" option, if enabled, forces strategic use of save states.
- It works for some platforms (e.g FXPAK) that would otherwise be unsupported.
This feature requires 256KB SRAM; FXPAK and most modern emulators support this configuration.

customize_settings.section: Seed page > Customization > Other customization options > Controller settings > Save state
customize_settings.label: Save state: Y
customize_settings.description:
This in-game save state option allows creating at most one save state at a time. A save state can be loaded an unlimited amount of times. Any save state is cleared automatically by a regular save (at a save station or the Ship).
- Unlimited: A save state can be created at any time.
- Limited: A save state can be created only once, until refreshed by a regular save or load.
Compared to emulator/platform-based save states, the in-game save state option has some advantages:
- Map tile progress is maintained.
- Music continues uninterrupted if the track is unchanged.
- Item collection times and other stats are preserved.
- The fact that save states are cleared by regular saves can help prevent accidental loads.
- The "Limited" option, if enabled, forces strategic use of save states.
- It works for some platforms (e.g FXPAK) that would otherwise be unsupported.
This feature requires 256KB SRAM; FXPAK and most modern emulators support this configuration.
